Title: Court overturns adoption order involving foreign national
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court in Penang has allowed the National Registration Department (NRD) to challenge a court order directing it to issue a birth certificate to an adopted Chinese citizen.
Judicial commissioner Suraiya Mustafa Kamal made the ruling after allowing NRD to become a party to an adoption appeal filed by a Malaysian man and his Chinese national wife, who sought to adopt the wife's niece.
She ruled that the earlier court order, dated March 17, was null and void on the grounds of illegality or lack of jurisdiction as it required NRD to act contrary to the Adoption Act and the Births and Deaths Registration Act.
Suraiya said the court retained the power to set aside the order even though it had been finalised, particularly when it contravened statutory requirements.
The case stemmed from an adoption application filed by the couple to adopt the wife's niece, who was born in Liaoning, China, on April 23, 2007.
The girl had been living with the couple in Penang since 2017 following the separation of her biological parents.
On Oct 17 last year, the George Town Sessions Court dismissed the couple's adoption application on the grounds that the girl did not possess a Malaysian birth certificate and that her ordinary residence had not been sufficiently established.
However, on March 17, High Court judge Dr Choong Yeow Choy allowed their appeal and granted the adoption order.
Choong ruled that foreign-born children without Malaysian birth certificates could still be adopted, provided the legal requirements were met and their welfare was protected.
The order also directed NRD to register the adoption and issue a birth certificate reflecting the girl's Chinese nationality and birthplace.
However, NRD challenged the order, arguing that it could not be implemented as the girl was not a Malaysian citizen and did not possess a birth certificate issued under the Births and Deaths Registration Act.
NRD filed an application on July 28 seeking to be added as a party to the proceedings and to set aside the March 17 order.
The couple raised a preliminary objection, arguing that NRD had no legal standing to challenge the order as it was not a party to the original proceedings.
They also argued that the High Court had no authority to revisit its earlier decision because the order had already been finalised.
However, Suraiya rejected both arguments.
She said NRD was directly affected by the order as it was the statutory authority responsible for issuing birth certificates.
"It is important that the applicant be named as a party from the beginning of the court's process as only the applicant is vested with the authority to perform and execute the March 17 order," she said in her written grounds of judgment dated Nov 16.
She also rejected the couple's argument that NRD's application was filed out of time, ruling that the delay did not prevent the department from challenging an unlawful order.
"The principle of justice dictates that justice should be done not only for the appellants or the child, who is not a Malaysian citizen, but justice should also be extended to all other affected parties," she said.
Lawyer Koay Ee Teng represented the couple, while federal counsel Nordiyanasari Omar appeared for NRD.
Koay said the case is now pending appeal at the Court of Appeal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Outside my knowledge': Jalaluddin responds to MB candidate issue
Article:
JELEBU: Negri Sembilan Umno Liaison Committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias said he was not informed of the sole menteri besar candidate submitted to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
He said the submission was made without his knowledge, stressing that it is the Umno president's prerogative to nominate a candidate for the post.
"It is outside my knowledge," he said when contacted today.
His remarks follow speculation linking the Pertang assemblyman and Jelebu member of parliament as the new menteri besar to replace Datuk Ismail Lasim, who reportedly resigned.
Yesterday, Deputy Prime Minister and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said only one
name had been submitted to Tuanku Muhriz
for royal assent.
Zahid was reported as saying that the letter proposing the candidate had been sent to the palace following Ismail's resignation.
Zahid, who is also Barisan Nasional chairman, said the coalition leaves the matter entirely to the ruler's discretion and consent.
It was reported yesterday that Jalaluddin was tipped to be appointed the new Negri Sembilan menteri besar, which would end the state's administrative crisis that has dragged on since August.
Rumours of Jalaluddin's appointment have been circulating strongly for the past two weeks.
Jalaluddin was previously reported to have been summoned for an audience with Tuanku Muhriz on Oct 9, sparking widespread speculation over the meeting.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chinese engineer pleads not guilty to endangering son at Nilai toll plaza
Article:
SEREMBAN: A Chinese citizen who went viral for allegedly leaving his child near the Nilai toll plaza pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to exposing the 12-year-old to the risk of physical injury.
Jiao Bo, 45, entered the plea after the charge was read out in Mandarin by an interpreter before judge Datin M. Kunasundary.
According to the charge, Jiao, an engineer, had exposed the child in a manner likely to cause physical injury at 1.21pm at the Nilai toll plaza exit ramp.
The charge was framed under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, which carries a maximum fine of RM50,000, up to 20 years' imprisonment, or both, upon conviction.
Earlier, deputy public prosecutor Siti Khairiah Abdul Razak offered no bail, citing the seriousness of the offence and the fact that the accused is the victim's father.
Siti Khairiah also informed the court that the child is currently in the mother's care.
Counsel Shahmi Iffah Mohd Arshad requested minimum bail, arguing that Jiao is the family's sole breadwinner.
He said the accused has lived in Malaysia for 10 years on a company-sponsored employment pass with his wife and two children, aged 12 and eight.
"The accused manages all family affairs, including banking and the children's schooling.
"This is his first offence, either in Malaysia or China, and his detention has caused distress to his wife and emotional trauma to the children after seeing their father arrested by police," he said.
Shahmi Iffah added that Jiao was willing to live separately from the family home in Cheras to ensure there was no risk to the child's safety.
The court allowed bail of RM20,000 with two Malaysian sureties aged 21 and above, and ordered the accused to surrender his passport and refrain from approaching or disturbing the victim.
The court fixed Dec 17 for mention and submission of the forensic report.
It was previously reported that a man was arrested after leaving his child near the Nilai toll plaza on the North-South Expressway, following a viral video of the incident.
Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya had said that an
argument between two siblings
inside the car angered the father, prompting him to allegedly leave one of them behind as a lesson.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar's defamation suit against Tuan Ibrahim to go to trial in May
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's
defamation suit
against Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man will go to trial next year.
Anwar's lawyer, Datuk Sankara Nair, said the five-day trial is scheduled for May 11 to 14 and May 28, with Dec 18 fixed for case management.
The dates were set before High Court Judicial Commissioner Moh Kok Wai during case management proceedings in chambers today.
Anwar filed the suit against Tuan Ibrahim in August.
Sankara said the suit stems from allegedly false and defamatory statements made by Tuan Ibrahim during a political speech at Felda Jenderak Utara, Kuala Krau, Pahang, on or around June 14.
He said the suit also relates to the publication and republication of the allegedly defamatory statements in video recordings and on social media platforms, including YouTube and Facebook, as well as on the defendant's Facebook account, "@Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man."
Sankara said the reliefs sought include general, aggravated and exemplary damages, as well as an injunction barring Tuan Ibrahim from making, publishing, republishing or disseminating the statements or any with a similar meaning.
He said Anwar is also seeking an order for the removal of the posts from social media accounts and platforms under Tuan Ibrahim's custody or control, alongside interest, costs and other relief deemed just by the court.
Anwar had previously issued a letter of demand to Tuan Ibrahim over the matter.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's Q3 economy expands faster than expected at 5.5pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 5.5 per cent in the third quarter of 2026, surpassing the advance estimate of 5.3 per cent.
Bank Negara Malaysia said the stronger growth was driven by sustained household spending, increased investment activities and improved export performance, particularly in technology-related products.
On the domestic front, household spending was supported by favourable labour market conditions and steady income growth.
The central bank said export growth strengthened further, driven by technology-related shipments of both electrical and electronics (E&E) and non-E&E products.
Bank Negara governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said Malaysia's E&E sector continued to benefit from strong global technology demand, supported by robust artificial intelligence-related investment.
"Reflecting this strength, domestic E&E exports accelerated to 66.9 per cent year-on-year growth in the third quarter.
"China, Singapore and the US remain Malaysia's top E&E export destinations, with exports to all three markets recording strong double-digit growth," he said at a joint press conference on Malaysia's third-quarter 2026 GDP performance.
Malaysia's economy expanded by 5.6 per cent in the first nine months of 2026, although third-quarter growth moderated from six per cent in the second quarter.
Rasheed said Malaysia's strong economic performance was expected to push full-year growth above five per cent in 2026.
He said the economy was well-positioned to sustain this momentum into 2027, supported by solid economic fundamentals and positive outcomes from ongoing structural reforms.
"Malaysia's economy is very likely to grow by up to five per cent in 2026 and between 4.2 per cent and 5.2 per cent in 2027, with domestic demand remaining a major driver of growth," he added.
Rasheed said the growth outlook remained subject to both upside and downside risks, including a further escalation of conflict in the Middle East and weaker-than-expected commodity production.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's current account surplus hits RM5.7bil in Q3
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's balance of payments remains in surplus in the third quarter of 2026, with the current account recording a surplus of RM5.7 billion.
This was supported by stronger goods exports despite widening deficits in services and primary income, according to the Statistics Department.
It said the goods account surplus expanded to RM56.2 billion from RM40.7 billion in the preceding quarter, as exports rose to RM409.7 billion from RM359.3 billion.
Export growth was underpinned by stronger demand for electrical and electronics (E&E) products, particularly those linked to artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, high-performance computing and advanced memory technologies, especially from the United States, Singapore and China.
However, the services account deficit widened sharply to RM6.9 billion from RM700 million in the second quarter.
Imports grew 17.9 per cent to RM97.3 billion, outpacing the 10.4 per cent increase in exports to RM90.4 billion.
The departmentvattributed the wider deficit mainly to other business services, which more than doubled to RM17 billion from RM8 billion, reflecting higher payments for professional and management consulting services, particularly in the E&E industry.
The primary income deficit also widened to RM41.8 billion from RM27.2 billion, driven by higher earnings of foreign companies operating in Malaysia, which reached RM64.3 billion during the quarter.
Meanwhile, the financial account reversed from a net outflow of RM27 billion in the preceding quarter to a net inflow of RM19.8 billion.
This was supported by stronger portfolio investment, other investment and direct investment flows.
Foreign direct investment (FDI) net inflows nearly doubled to RM14.3 billion from RM7.4 billion in the second quarter, reflecting improved business performance among foreign-owned companies, with higher profits retained for future expansion.
The services sector, particularly information and communication activities related to data centres, was the largest recipient of FDI, followed by manufacturing and mining and quarrying.
Singapore, Hong Kong and the United States were the leading sources of FDI during the quarter.
In contrast, direct investment abroad (DIA) recorded a slightly higher net outflow of RM7.6 billion against RM7 billion previously.
Investments were mainly channelled into mining and quarrying, followed by financial activities.
Saudi Arabia, the Netherlands and Thailand were the main destinations for Malaysian investments abroad.
On the international investment position, Malaysia's accumulated FDI position stood at RM1.23 trillion at end-September 2026, while its DIA position reached RM639.7 billion.
The country's total international financial assets amounted to RM2.89 trillion against liabilities of RM2.93 trillion, resulting in a net international investment liability position of RM36 billion.
International reserves stood at RM537.6 billion at the end of September.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Myanmar mother among 9 migrants arrested in Kelantan
Article:
KOTA BARU: A Myanmar mother who returned to Malaysia illegally in search of work to support her family was arrested with two friends after crossing the border from Thailand into Kelantan.
Known only as Erika, the 30-year-old had been working as a cook at a restaurant in Puchong without valid documents since last year.
The mother of a toddler said she had paid a Thai agent RM3,000 to arrange her journey from Tak Bai, Thailand, to Selangor.
After returning to Myanmar last month, she decided to come back to Malaysia to resume her job, bringing two friends, aged 18 and 28, with her.
However, all three were arrested in Tumpat yesterday after entering the country illegally.
They were among nine undocumented migrants detained by police.
Erika said it was her first arrest.
"I know I have broken the law, but I have no other choice. I need to find work in Malaysia to support my family.
"I brought two close friends with me this time, but unfortunately, all three of us ended up facing the same fate," she said.
Myanmar has been gripped by conflict and economic hardship since the military seized power in a 2021 coup, prompting many people to seek work abroad, including in Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar calls for fairer trade, technology sharing at Apec CEO Summit
Article:
SHENZHEN: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told global and business leaders today there was a need for genuine multilateralism, equitable technology sharing and human-centric development.
Speaking at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit 2026 at the Qianhai International Convention Centre, the prime minister said global leaders and the business community must ensure economic progress does not marginalise emerging economies.
Stressing the need for a fairer global economic architecture, he said true international cooperation cannot be one-sided.
"We must respect multilateral arrangements. You cannot, with one voice, claim to promote trade and investment, but restrict it only to your own country," he said.
"The entire multilateral framework must change; we have entered into a new era of assertiveness. Small and emerging countries must be treated with respect and dignity."
Earlier, Chinese President Xi Jinping opened the summit with a pledge to open China's market to more global products and services while upholding multilateralism and the rule of law.
In his opening speech, Xi said China would not only cut tariffs and expand market access for global producers, but also reform rules, regulations and standards to ease entry into its 1.4 billion-strong market.
Positioning Malaysia as a key trading nation expanding investments from both the United States and China, Anwar commended Beijing's leadership for opening its markets to the world.
He said the current geopolitical climate requires advanced nations to go beyond offering market access, urging them to share their experiences and technological breakthroughs — particularly in sectors such as semiconductors and artificial intelligence — with developing nations.
Anwar reminded corporate leaders that emerging economies, many of which endured decades of colonialism and oppression, need these investments to revitalise their economies.
Reiterating the importance of Asean centrality, he said powerful countries cannot impose their circumstances on smaller nations, adding that trade and investment must uplift broader societies rather than serve isolated geopolitical interests.
Turning to the corporate sector, Anwar underscored the business community's vital role in shaping the Asia-Pacific region's future.
He challenged CEOs to look beyond immediate commercial success and immediate profit margins, reminding them that the partnerships they forge and the technologies they develop carry a profound social responsibility.
The ultimate goal of corporate investment, he noted, should be to strengthen domestic economies and develop human capital so that emerging economies can move up the value chain.
"The true measure of economic progress must ultimately be found in the lives it transforms," Anwar concluded, setting forth a vision for the Asia-Pacific where nations retain the freedom to chart their own destinies.
Achieving this, he warned, will require immense political courage and a rejection of growth models that lead to further inequity and neglect, ensuring that the wealth and wisdom of the region are shared by all.
The Apec CEO Summit 2026 is part of the Apec Economic Leaders' Week taking place in Shenzhen from Nov 12 to 20, drawing more than 2,000 business and political representatives from 21 Apec and 13 non-Apec economies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MP flags environmental, water concerns over Kapar industrial park
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An opposition member of parliament (MP) has asked whether the government had assessed the combined impact of a planned 1,623-acre industrial development in Bukit Kerayong, Kapar, on flooding, water supply, electricity and infrastructure.
Dr Halimah Ali (PN-Kapar) raised the concerns in a supplementary question to Deputy Digital Minister Datuk Wilson Ugak Kumbong in the Dewan Rakyat.
She asked whether an assessment had been carried out to ensure the project would not worsen flooding or increase the risk of overflow because of changes in land use.
Halimah said Kapar already faced infrastructure problems, including overcrowded schools, recurring floods, damaged roads and pressure on its drainage system.
She also asked whether the government could ensure residents would not bear the social and environmental costs of the project while others benefited from the investment.
According to a YTL Power International statement issued on Oct 29, the company had entered into a joint venture with SD Guthrie and Bumi Assets to develop the industrial site.
An online report said MBSB Research had not ruled out the possibility of a large-scale data centre campus being part of the development.
Ugak said the Data Centre Task Force assessed every data centre application to ensure adequate electricity and water supplies before approval.
He said the assessments were carried out in coordination with utility providers and relevant technical agencies.
The government also assessed energy efficiency through Power Usage Effectiveness and encouraged the use of renewable energy and more efficient technology, he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar thanks Trump for recognising Malaysia's role in easing Cambodia-Thailand tensions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed appreciation for United States President Donald Trump's recognition of Malaysia's efforts in helping Thailand and Cambodia ease tensions and pursue peace.
Anwar shared this in a Facebook post today regarding his participation in the Asean-United States Special Summit.
"The commitment of both countries to continue dialogue is crucial to ensuring lasting peace along the border and stability in our region," he said.
Earlier, Trump acknowledged Anwar's role in helping broker a peace agreement between Cambodia and Thailand last year, while reaffirming Washington's commitment to its full implementation.
Speaking at the Asean-United States Special Summit in Manila last night, Trump said joint efforts by him and Anwar had secured a ceasefire and enabled displaced residents to return home.
Anwar said the meeting also provided an opportunity to strengthen Asean's cooperation with the United States in areas of mutual interest, including trade, investment and technology.
"This relationship must continue to be strengthened, with a focus on benefits that the people can tangibly experience," he said.
Anwar also attended a dinner hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. in his capacity as Asean chair, which marked the conclusion of the 49th Asean Summit, before departing for Shenzhen.
He expressed his appreciation to Marcos and the Philippine government for their chairmanship, describing it as a source of pride for all Asean citizens.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Xi and Putin to meet ahead of historic Trump trilateral summit
Article:
SHENZHEN: Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin were set to meet on Wednesday, a day ahead of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump in Shenzhen.
Thursday's trilateral summit has triggered fears that the three powerful men could decide the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv and Europe, and seek to carve up the world into 21st-century spheres of influence.
Washington had signalled that Ukraine was not expected to be addressed — something Xi vehemently sees as not China's problem — before Trump said it would be.
China has said only that the leaders would hold "in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations" on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) meeting.
Also up for discussion are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.
Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.
In from the cold
Putin, who arrived in Shenzhen early on Wednesday, has been shunned by the West since launching Europe's worst conflict since World War II with his 2022 attack on Ukraine.
Xi and Putin were both due to address the Apec gathering before discussing energy and finance and then, in a smaller format, foreign policy, including Ukraine and North Korea, Russian officials said.
Xi on Wednesday called for greater international cooperation on AI and free trade.
"Starting by lowering tariffs, expanding access and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform," Xi said.
[[nid:1580282]]
Kim incoming?
Trump was still in the Philippines on Wednesday, where he had met fellow Quad leaders Australia, Japan and India a day earlier.
He said he was eyeing one-on-one talks with Putin and possibly North Korea's Kim Jong Un at his next stop in Shenzhen.
He added that Kim "would like" to meet in China, hours after Beijing said it had no information about an encounter between the two.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday stopped short of confirming a meeting with Kim.
"If we have a problem with North Korea, the only way we're ever going to solve it is if we engage with them," Rubio said in Manila.
Trump's Quad meeting at the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit was the security alliance's first since his return to power in January 2025.
The grouping is broadly aimed at counterbalancing China's regional influence.
Trump's visit to the Philippines saw protests by around 2,000 people carrying banners reading "Trump out now" and "Reject Pax Silica" — a reference to a US supply chain initiative.
[[nid:1580281]]
Tariffs, chips and rare earths
While Asean leaders grappled with a raft of regional issues, the spectre of Trump's ongoing tariff blitz loomed large.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a "countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism" while touting Beijing's expanding trade with the bloc.
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Canada's Mark Carney struck a similar note on trade, with both explicitly citing the need to reduce their dependence on the US market.
On Tuesday, a combative Trump showed no let-up in his trade war with Beijing, saying the United States would catch up with China in rare earths production "within 10 months".
Hours before Trump touched down in Manila, Washington announced new rules on the transfer of advanced AI chips, a move that could potentially rankle Asean members.
Companies shipping high-end chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia will now require a special licence, as the countries were said to represent a "higher-than-normal risk of diversion".
Singapore responded by saying it was exploring ways to facilitate "trusted access" for firms based in the city-state.
Pax Silica
Trump was set to meet Philippine leader Ferdinand Marcos at the presidential palace on Wednesday before heading to Shenzhen.
Aimed at countering China's dominance in semiconductors and rare earths, the initiative has been the focus of months of protests in the Philippines as it threatens to displace Indigenous families.
"We are gathered here today to call for the stop of Pax Silica and to save the lands of the Filipino people," Mariposa, a 21-year-old drag queen, told AFP at Tuesday's protest while wearing a long black cape emblazoned with the words "Pax Silica Sashay Away!"
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China's Xi calls for greater international cooperation on AI
Article:
SHENZHEN: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for greater international cooperation on AI and free trade, as pressure grows on world powers to do more to address the risks of the groundbreaking technology.
Xi made the remarks as he formally opened an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, where he is expected to meet US President Donald Trump on Thursday.
"We should actively build partnerships for scientific and technological innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence and promote a green and low-carbon transition," the Chinese leader said.
"By continuously transforming our innovation strengths into growth momentum, we can provide a robust impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and foster shared prosperity across the region."
Xi also called for the elimination of trade and investment barriers, saying that it was crucial to "promote inclusive and balanced development".
He said China sought to "provide a more stable, predictable and beneficial environment for global enterprises" and would continue to expand access in its manufacturing and services sectors.
"Starting by lowering tariffs, expanding access and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform," Xi said.
Trade tensions have been looming over the leaders of the world's two largest economies as the summit approaches.
Trump has upended the global trade order by imposing wide-ranging tariffs on many countries, which China has met head-on with counter-levies and threats to withhold crucial exports.
On the sidelines of last year's APEC summit in South Korea, Trump and Xi reached a tenuous truce in their trade war, but it will expire in January.
The United States this week announced tougher restrictions on the export to China of advanced semiconductors used to train and run AI models, controls it says are needed for national security.
The new US rules crack down not only on chip smuggling but also on the large grey market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres in third countries full of chips designed by the Californian giant Nvidia.
Nvidia on Wednesday reported blockbuster earnings but the results were overshadowed by a widening scandal sparked by former CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman suspected by US officials of spying for China.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nvidia says no return for ousted CEO, reports revenue boom
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: US chip giant Nvidia on Tuesday ruled out any comeback for ousted CEO Jensen Huang, who was forced out in a spy scandal, and reported that it had doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than $115 billion, beating expectations.
Huang sought to be reinstated despite resigning last week over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, but his successor – interim CEO Colette Kress – said that it was now "business as usual" at the company as it charts a way ahead without him.
Harvey Jones, the chair of the company's board, said in an earnings call that "the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."
Investors scoured the upbeat results for evidence that the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the Nvidia crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.
"Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people," Kress said in her first remarks since being appointed by the board last week.
She forecast stronger revenue growth of 75 percent in next fiscal year, up from 70 percent.
Huang's bid on Tuesday to get his job back was the latest twist for the company at the center of an AI boom that has propelled markets to record highs and boosted global economic growth.
The recent upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia – which has lost $700 billion in market value since the scandal broke – and Huang is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns.
A charismatic promoter of AI, his fall triggered immediate calls from Elon Musk and others for his return, and even President Donald Trump said he "would not mind" seeing Huang back at Nvidia, downplaying the espionage allegations.
- Battle over AI chips -
"Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," Huang said, hours before the earnings release.
"If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."
As the spy scandal deepened, Washington on Monday announced new restrictions on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing.
The new US export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over talks between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which starts this week in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.
Under Washington's new rules, data centers anywhere in the world will need a US license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.
The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil – countries the US Commerce Department says present a "higher-than-normal risk of diversion" of the chips.
The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.
While the loophole has been known to authorities, the revelation of Huang's affair has drawn intense scrutiny to the practice.
His lover Alice Huang, who is not related to the 63-year-old, is a former executive of Megaspeed – a Singapore-based cloud computing firm under US criminal investigation for allegedly helping Chinese companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips in circumvention of export controls.
Investors are watching for signs of whether Kress will slow Huang's aggressive investment strategy, which saw him commit tens of billions of dollars to AI companies.
Huang on Tuesday sounded a note of contrition in his statement, saying "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police van tragedy highlights need for stronger vehicle safety
Article:
I AM deeply saddened by the
tragic accident involving a police van
near Tapah on the North-South Expressway, which claimed the life of 26-year-old Lance Corporal Muhammad Shahrul Alif Yaacob and left 10 other police personnel injured.
My heartfelt condolences go to the family of the deceased. I also wish the injured personnel a speedy and full recovery.
This tragedy is a painful reminder that road safety must extend to everyone, including those who serve and protect the public. Police personnel travelling on official duties must be assured that the vehicles they use are safe, roadworthy and properly maintained.
While preliminary investigations suggest that a sudden burst of the van's rear tyre may have caused the accident, the incident raises several important questions that deserve serious attention.
First, there must be a comprehensive review of the maintenance and inspection procedures for police vehicles, particularly those used for long-distance journeys. Tyres, braking systems, steering mechanisms and other critical components must be inspected regularly and systematically.
Second, the safety of police personnel travelling in official vehicles must be given priority. Proper seating arrangements, functioning seat belts and compliance with vehicle passenger capacity are essential safeguards.
Third, there should be a thorough investigation into the accident to establish all contributing factors, beyond the preliminary finding of a burst tyre. The findings should be used to identify weaknesses and prevent similar tragedies.
I also believe that occupational safety and health principles must be given greater emphasis within enforcement agencies. Police personnel are exposed to occupational risks not only when confronting criminals or performing enforcement duties but also when travelling in vehicles as part of their work.
Their safety must therefore be recognised as an important component of workplace safety and health management.
The tragedy should prompt police and other enforcement agencies to undertake a comprehensive safety audit of their vehicle fleets and strengthen preventive maintenance and operational safety procedures.
We must not wait for another life to be lost before taking corrective action.
Every life matters, including the lives of those who dedicate themselves to protecting our communities. Their safety must never be taken for granted.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
SAFETY ADVOCATE
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perlis detects illegal female-only e-hailing services
Article:
PADANG BESAR: The Road Transport Department (RTD) in Perlis has detected illegal e-hailing services operated by female drivers exclusively for passengers of the same gender.
Its director, Noraini Mohd Nawi, said the services were being widely promoted on social media platforms such as Telegram and Threads.
She said two cases involving female drivers were detected and action taken during monitoring and enforcement operations between January and October.
During the same period, the department issued 31 notices for various offences related to illegal passenger transport services and seized 14 vehicles.
The offences involved misuse of a Motor Vehicle Licence under Section 23(2) of the Road Transport Act 1987. The courts imposed total fines of RM14,000.
Noraini was speaking at a press conference after an RTD operation around the Padang Besar Roundabout yesterday.
She said the department took the matter seriously as unlicensed passenger transport services violated the law and left passengers without insurance protection in the event of an accident.
On a separate issue, Noraini said the department had stepped up enforcement against drivers and vehicles registered in Thailand operating in Perlis.
Between January and October, the department issued 1,068 notices and seized 16 Thai-registered vehicles for various traffic offences.
Offences involving tinted windows accounted for the highest number, with 347 notices, followed by technical offences (211), driving without a licence (84), vehicle licensing offences (37) and other offences (361).
From 2025 to October this year, enforcement against vehicles from Thailand resulted in RM257,430 in collections from summonses, including payments of outstanding fines, she said.
Two vehicles from Thailand were also seized during the period.

Title: Heavy rain triggers floods in 23 areas across Selangor
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Heavy rainfall, with recorded levels ranging from 63.5mm to 114.5mm, triggered floods in 23 areas across four districts in Selangor yesterday.
The affected districts were Klang, with 8 areas, followed by Gombak (7), Kuala Selangor (5) and Petaling (3).
The Selangor Drainage and Irrigation Department said Kuala Selangor recorded the highest rainfall at 114.5mm in Kampung Merbau Indah Tambahan and Perumahan Saujana Aman.
"In Klang, the affected areas included Kampung Delek and Kampung Rantau Panjang, which each recorded 95.5mm of rainfall, followed by Kampung Jalan Kebun at 94.5mm.
"In Gombak, Pekan Batu Arang and Jalan Tasik Puteri-Batu Arang (Jalan Lembah Hijau) each recorded 84.5mm.
"In Petaling, Kampung Kubu Gajah recorded 79mm, followed by Kampung Budiman, Shah Alam (73.5mm) and Lorong Keluli 1C, i-City (69mm)," it said in a statement.
The department said 353 sluice gates and 161 permanent pumps remained operational to channel floodwaters into rivers.
It added that 141 mobile emergency pumps had been installed and were operating in nine districts, while another nine units remained on standby for deployment to critical locations if necessary.
"Selangor JPS remains vigilant in monitoring flood incidents and continues to take measures to minimise their impact and risks in affected areas.
"We will also continue regular maintenance work before, during and after floods to ensure that rivers and drainage systems under our jurisdiction function properly to channel floodwaters towards the sea.
"The public can obtain the latest flood information through the JPS Malaysia Public InfoBanjir portal at https://publicinfobanjir.water.gov.my/?lang=en or the Selangor JPS InfoBanjir portal at https://infobanjirjps.selangor.gov.my/index.html," it said.
Several areas were hit by flash floods yesterday following heavy rain that began at noon.
In Shah Alam, the Klang District Disaster Management Committee chairman declared a Level 1 disaster following flooding in Kampung Jalan Kebun.
A Level 1 disaster refers to an incident that can be controlled and managed by the authorities at district level.
Shah Alam City Council (MBSA), in a social media post, said a temporary relief centre (PPS) had been opened at Masjid An-Naim in Jalan Kebun to accommodate residents affected by the floods.
"The centre began operating today to provide shelter for affected residents and ensure their safety and welfare," it said.

Title: 99 Speed Mart shares rise on firmer Q3 earnings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd shares rose in early trading after a strong performance in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 2026).
At 10.15 am, the counter rose eight sen to RM3.04, with 24,477 shares traded.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia yesterday, the company said its net profit rose to RM189.78 million in Q3 2026 from RM163.24 million in the corresponding quarter last year.
Revenue increased 8.7 per cent to RM3.3 billion from RM3.03 billion a year earlier, driven by continued expansion of its retail networks, it said.
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB IB) expects 99 Speed Mart's steady sales volume growth to be sustained, supported by its staples-oriented product mix and highly accessible outlet locations.
"Other than that, 99 Speed Mart is well-positioned to continue capitalising on the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah programme, with around 3,000 outlets being empanelled – with such contributions accounting for a steady five per cent of total sales.
"Beyond the near term, earnings growth should be anchored by the company's strategies to expand its addressable market through diversifying sourcing channels to broaden its product offerings (namely, electrical appliances and additional over-the-counter drugs), developing its bulk sales platform, and expanding its presence beyond Malaysia," it said in a note.
RHB IB maintained its "Buy" recommendation, with a lower revised target price of RM3.67 from RM4.02.

Title: Bank of Japan governor says central bank should keep raising rates
Article:
TOKYO: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Wednesday the central bank should continue raising interest rates while stressing the need to anchor underlying inflation around its 2.0 per cent target.
Speaking in parliament, Ueda said it was important to see underlying inflation anchored around 2.0 per cent over time and conduct monetary policy appropriately to ensure that this could be achieved.
"Given that financial conditions are still accommodative, it would be appropriate to continue raising the policy rate and adjust the degree of monetary easing in line with developments in the economy, prices and financial conditions," Ueda said.
The BOJ kept interest rates steady at 1.25 per cent at its October 30 meeting but declared victory in its 14-year battle to hit its price target and stressed its policy had entered a new phase focused on avoiding an inflation overshoot, reinforcing its hawkish bias.
Ueda said the planned consumption tax cut on food would likely support economic growth by boosting households' real purchasing power, though the size of the impact would depend on factors such as companies' pricing behaviour and consumer sentiment.
Once the details of the measure are finalised, the central bank will assess its impact on underlying inflation and reflect that analysis in future policy decisions, he added.
Asked about the possibility of emergency bond-buying operations, Ueda said the BOJ would make a comprehensive assessment based on conditions at the time, including whether serious disruptions to market functioning had emerged and required a policy response.
He also cautioned against using such operations to contain long-term yields, saying the move could prove counterproductive if markets perceive the BOJ as helping finance government spending. "In that case, long-term interest rates could become even more volatile," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rubber tapper couple's dream inspires 46 doctors across four generations
Article:
MUAR: The death of their second child from a high fever became a turning point for a rubber tapper couple, inspiring them to encourage their other children to pursue careers in medicine.
The dream of the late Loo Siew Chin and her husband, Lim Tang Too, grew into a remarkable family legacy, with eight of their 11 children becoming doctors.
Today, 46 doctors across four generations carry on that legacy, alongside 15 spouses, bringing the extended family total to 61.
Their eldest son, Datuk Dr Lim Boon Sho, 81, said 34 of them are specialists serving in Malaysia and abroad, including in the United Kingdom, Australia, Ireland and Scotland.
Recalling their journey, Boon Sho said his parents were particularly proud when he secured a scholarship at 17 to study medicine in India, followed by seven of his younger siblings.
"My late parents always encouraged us to pursue careers in medicine not just for our own benefit, but more importantly, to serve the community so that the loss of family members due to a lack of proper medical treatment would not happen again," said the former Sungai Bakap state assemblyman.
The family's story came to light following Loo's death at the age of 104 on Nov 12. She was laid to rest at the Trinity Church Muar Cemetery on Monday.
[[nid:1580298]]
Also sharing their experiences were six of Boon Sho's siblings: Dr Lim Boon Sin, 77; Dr Lim Boon Ben, 75; Dr Lim Boon Seng, 73; Dr Lim Boon Hock, 68; Dr Lim Boon Han, 64; and Karin Lim Ai Ching, 66, a lawyer.
The couple's fourth child, Boon Seng, said one of his most unforgettable memories was fleeing their home in Serom with his parents following an attack by communist insurgents, before being taken in by a Malay woman they fondly called Aunty.
"At the time, we stayed in a hut she owned, and Jalan Serkam became the place where we grew up. It was there that our parents began running a small business.
"Although our family was quite poor, to the extent that even a loaf of bread or a packet of fried noodles had to be shared, our mother was always kind to others. Anyone who came to our home would never leave empty-handed," he said.
He added that his parents also had four adopted children, two of whom became doctors.
The couple's seventh child, Boon Han, said they were taught from a young age to always do good, help those in need and refrain from hurting others.
"One of our mother's pieces of advice that we will remember for the rest of our lives was to be generous, never look down on others and never cheat. These are the values we have held on to throughout our lives and have contributed to our success. She also reminded us that whether in good times or bad, our family must always remain united and help one another.
"Our mother was everything to us, and among the things we will remember following her passing is her favourite meal of rice porridge served with pickled vegetables and homemade salted eggs," he said.

Title: Tuanku Muhriz tells Ismail to continue as MB, resignation undecided [WATCH]
Article:
SEREMBAN: The position of Datuk Ismail Lasim as Negri Sembilan menteri besar remains unresolved after he had an audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Hinggap yesterday.
Ismail arrived at the palace at about 5pm, and the meeting lasted more than an hour.
The vehicle carrying Tuanku Muhriz was seen leaving Istana Hinggap through the main entrance at about 6.30pm.
It is understood that Tuanku Muhriz instructed Ismail to continue carrying out his duties and responsibilities as menteri besar.
The development suggests that Ismail's position remains unchanged, although the palace has yet to issue an official statement confirming the outcome of the meeting.
State government agencies also continued to identify Ismail as Negri Sembilan menteri besar at official events he attended or officiated.
[[nid:1580301]]
Questions, however, remain over a resignation letter attributed to Ismail, the authenticity of which has yet to be confirmed.
BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said a copy of the letter had been submitted to the palace in a social media post at 10pm on Monday.
Earlier, the Negri Sembilan Palace, in a statement issued by Royal Comptroller Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali, said a menteri besar's resignation would only take effect after receiving Tuanku Muhriz's consent, in accordance with the Negri Sembilan State Constitution.
The palace also said the authenticity of the resignation letter attributed to Ismail had yet to be verified.
On Monday, BN chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had received a copy of the resignation letter, which was purportedly addressed to Tuanku Muhriz, Zambry said.
Ismail, a senior state Umno leader, was sworn in as Negri Sembilan menteri besar on Aug 2 after BN won 18 state assembly seats and Perikatan Nasional secured seven in the state election, allowing the two coalitions to form the state government with a two-thirds majority.

Title: Education Ministry receives 73,498 Year One applications from six-year-olds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry received 73,498 applications for Year One admission under the 2027 Academic Calendar from six-year-olds as at Sept 30.
The figure forms part of the total 491,649 applications received for Year One admission next year, including 418,151 applications from seven-year-old children.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the ministry had decided to expand access to Year One by allowing parents to enrol their six-year-old children from the 2027 Academic Calendar.
She said the policy was voluntary and based on parental choice, while admission for seven-year-olds would remain the primary pathway throughout the transition period.
"The ministry's priority is to give parents the option based on their children's individual readiness, while ensuring the education system has the capacity and preparedness to accommodate six-year-olds who opt to enter Year One," she said in a written parliamentary reply published on the parliament website.
She was responding to Manndzri Nasib (BN-Tenggara), who asked how many six-year-old children had registered for Year One.
Manndzri also asked whether the ministry was confident that the voluntary policy would receive an overwhelming response from parents, or whether it was a rushed experiment that could eventually place an emotional burden on pupils and teachers.
Fadhlina said the ministry would continue monitoring registration trends and the preparedness of individual schools.
This would include coordinating student placements, teacher requirements, classroom capacity and infrastructure.
"These measures will ensure Year One operations under the 2027 Academic Calendar run smoothly and provide a conducive learning environment without compromising pupils' access to and the quality of education," she said.

Title: US export curbs threaten to delay Malaysia's data centre projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's construction sector could face delays in data centre-related contract awards following new United States export controls, although local contractors have limited direct exposure to projects involving entities from D5 countries.
According to CIMB Securities, ground checks indicated that most listed Malaysian contractors had limited direct involvement in turnkey data centre construction projects involving D5-country entities, reducing the risk of outright project cancellations.
"Nevertheless, we believe the new US export controls may rekindle concerns over the pace of future data centre-related contract awards for the sector," it said in a note.
Following the announcement of the proposed US AI diffusion ruling in Jan 2025, CIMB Securities observed a roughly six-month delay in data cente-related contract flows as end clients adopted a wait-and-see approach.
Among the big three Malaysian contractors, it noted that Sunway Construction Group Bhd has the highest exposure to data centre projects, which account for 70 per cent of the company's RM10.5 billion outstanding order book as of Jun 30, 2026.
In comparison, the firm said IJM Corp Bhd and Gamuda Bhd have outstanding DC contributions accounting for RM2.8 billion (14 per cent) and RM8.8 billion (19 per cent) of their respective outstanding order books.
"Separately, we posit that the pace of data centre-affiliated grid connection projects could moderate in the near-term as heightened compliance requirements delay customer onboarding and overall capacity deployment," it said.
CIMB Securities has maintained its 'Neutral' call on the sector.
Conversely, the firm said more measured US data centre buildouts could create supply gaps that redirect incremental AI infrastructure investments towards Asean over the longer term, with Malaysia standing out for its geopolitical neutrality and maturing data centre ecosystem.
"Gamuda is our top sector pick for its diversified earnings and international exposure," it added.

Title: High Court: Developers cannot escape liability for recurring defects
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Property developers cannot escape liability for construction defects even after the defect liability period (DLP) has expired, the High Court has ruled.
Judge Sumathi Murugiah made the ruling after finding that Astana Modal (M) Sdn Bhd had failed to effectively rectify recurring water leaks and related damage in luxury homes at D'Island Residence in Puchong.
She said developers remained responsible for poor workmanship despite having carried out repairs, particularly when defects persisted or recurred.
"Astana's earlier rectification works and the expiry of the DLP do not provide a complete defence where the water leakage remained or recurred because the repairs were ineffective.
"I therefore find that the plaintiffs have proven that Astana breached its obligation to construct and deliver the affected properties in a good and workmanlike manner," she said in her grounds of judgment delivered yesterday.
The ruling followed two lawsuits against Astana involving 69 purchasers of 41 semi-detached and super-linked houses, as well as two other purchasers of a double-storey house in the same development.
The purchasers claimed that their properties had numerous defects, including cracks, water leaks, staining, uneven finishes and alleged structural deficiencies.
Although Astana had carried out repairs on several occasions, some defects persisted or recurred, prompting the purchasers to take legal action.
Sumathi said the recurring defects were concerning, given that the properties had been marketed as luxury homes and sold at high prices.
"Given that the properties were marketed as luxury homes and sold for high prices, it is impossible to ignore the recurring occurrence of defects.
"Defects may ordinarily arise during the DLP and be remedied by the developer.
"However, the defects in the present case were not isolated complaints confined to the DLP.
"Some of them recurred despite Astana's previous attempts to rectify them and continued to appear even after the DLP had expired," she said.
She said Astana's own structural expert had also accepted that damage to plaster ceilings caused by water leaks was uncommon in a five-year-old building.
Sumathi said developers could not rely on an "as is where is" clause in a sale and purchase agreement to avoid liability for hidden defects or poor workmanship.
However, she dismissed the purchasers' claims that their homes were structurally unsafe or unfit for occupation.
She said they had failed to provide sufficiently reliable technical evidence to prove that the concrete used in the properties did not meet the required Grade C25 specification.
Grade C25 refers to concrete designed to withstand a compressive strength of 25 megapascals (MPa), a specification commonly used for structural components such as beams, columns and floor slabs.
Sumathi also dismissed their claims seeking to invalidate the Certificates of Completion and Compliance (CCCs) issued for the properties.
The court ordered Astana to pay the reasonable costs of rectifying recurring water leaks and the resulting damage to the affected properties.
The amount is to be calculated based on rectification quotations submitted during the trial, before the court order is filed.
The court also awarded the purchasers RM35,000 in legal costs.
Other claims, including refunds of the property purchase prices, expert fees, separate negligence damages, general damages for distress, aggravated damages and exemplary damages, were dismissed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US AI chip curbs threaten YTL Power's data centre growth, CIMB warns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tighter United States (US) restrictions on access to advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips could slow future data centre capacity expansion at YTL Power International Bhd, potentially weighing on its earnings forecasts, although its existing contracted capacity is expected to remain unaffected.
CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said the new US rules could constrain demand from data centre end-users headquartered in countries of concern, including China, although the impact would depend on how strictly the regulations are enforced and their implications for existing customers.
The firm said its base case assumed YTL Power's existing 298 megawatts (MW) of contracted co-location data centre capacity in Kulai, Johor, would remain intact, given its understanding that the lease agreements with tenants were firm.
However, it noted that future demand from restricted end-users could weaken, potentially slowing the pace of new capacity additions.
CIMB Securities estimated that if future capacity additions were halved to 100 MW annually from its current assumption of 200 MW, YTL Power's total contracted capacity would reach 678 MW by end-2030, compared with its current forecast of 1,078 MW.
Under this scenario, its core net profit forecasts for the financial years ending 2028 and 2029 would be four to nine per cent lower, while its fair value estimate would decline to RM5.03.
The firm said its financial year 2027 (FY27) earnings forecast would remain unchanged.
CIMB Securities also assessed a more severe scenario in which 60 to 70 per cent of YTL Power's existing contracted capacity, assumed to be linked to potentially restricted end-users, fell to zero.
This would reduce its core net profit forecasts for FY27 to FY29 by 12 to 15 per cent and lower its sum-of-parts-based fair value estimate to RM5.06.
If both existing capacity contracted by restricted end-users were removed and future capacity additions halved, the earnings impact would be greater, with core net profit forecasts falling by 14 to 20 per cent for FY27 to FY29 and fair value declining to RM4.05.
Nevertheless, CIMB Securities said weaker demand from restricted end-users could be partly offset by stronger demand from US hyperscalers and AI companies, particularly if the outcome of the recent US midterm elections resulted in a policy environment that made new data centre developments in the US more challenging.
The US Department of Commerce is establishing new restrictions requiring licences for the export, re-export or transfer of advanced AI chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, with exemptions for shipments destined for US companies.
Cloud service providers already supplying significant computing power to companies headquartered in countries of concern before the rule's publication must obtain licences within 90 days to continue providing those services, failing which they could face future export restrictions.
CIMB Securities maintained its "Buy" recommendation on YTL Power with an unchanged sum-of-parts-based target price of RM6.10, pending further clarification from the company.
It identified lower-than-expected growth in contracted data centre capacity as a key downside risk.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's semiconductor sector to weather US-China tech tensions, says PublicInvest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's semiconductor sector is expected to remain resilient amid escalating United States (US)-China technology tensions, according to Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest).
Analyst Chong Hoe Leong said companies with diversified customer exposure and capabilities in precision engineering, automated testing and inspection were better positioned to navigate the changing regulatory environment.
However, local graphics processing unit (GPU) server assemblers could face tighter regulatory scrutiny as delays to data centre projects potentially emerge from the latest US export-control measures.
"We view the latest measures as a structural tightening of the US semiconductor export-control regime rather than an isolated regulatory adjustment.
"This could potentially increase the cost of operating AI infrastructure in Southeast Asia, particularly for businesses with customers or ultimate beneficiaries linked to China," he said in a note.
The US administration has introduced additional restrictions to prevent Chinese companies from circumventing existing semiconductor export controls by accessing advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips through overseas data centres.
Previously, Chinese technology companies barred from directly purchasing high-performance US-designed AI chips could still obtain computing capacity by renting servers in third countries, including Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
The latest measures seek to close this indirect access channel, further tightening Washington's semiconductor export-control framework.
Chon said companies prohibited from directly purchasing high-performance US-designed AI chips, including those with 16 nodes and below, could still access computing capacity through server rentals, albeit using more mature-node technologies.
Meanwhile, Chinese semiconductor players such as Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp (SMIC), JCET Group and Tongfu Microelectronics could benefit from additional orders as China seeks to strengthen its domestic semiconductor capabilities.
He noted that China is also pursuing alternative approaches to sustain its AI development momentum, including AI model distillation, which involves using outputs from larger, more sophisticated AI models to train smaller and more cost-efficient domestic alternatives.
Chong said the latest restrictions create a policy dilemma for Beijing ahead of the meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on Nov 18 and 19.
"For local semiconductor companies, the key concern is whether licensing requirements will eventually extend to a wider range of tech equipment and manufacturing technologies," he said.
Nevertheless, Chong said the recent sell-off appeared to have overreacted to negative global developments.
PublicInvest maintained its "Overweight" stance on the sector, citing the ability of companies with diversified customer bases and specialised engineering capabilities to navigate the changing environment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hap Seng Plantations earnings set for Q4 lift despite softer palm oil prices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hap Seng Plantations Bhd is expected to record flat-to-slightly higher earnings in the fourth quarter (Q4) of financial year 2026 (FY26), as peak fresh fruit bunch (FFB) production is likely to be partly offset by lower average selling prices (ASPs).
RHB Research said Hap Seng Plantations's FFB output rose 11 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) and five per cent year-on-year (YoY) in Q3 FY26, supported by seasonally higher production despite drier weather conditions during the quarter.
On a year-to-date basis, the firm noted that FFB output for the 10 months ended October 2026 (10M26) grew 5.9 per cent YoY, trailing the company's full-year FY26 growth target of 9.2 per cent and its forecast of 7.1 per cent.
"However, we expect output to pick up in the remaining months as management guides for production to peak in Q4 2026, and monsoon rains should support the production.
"We therefore maintain our FY26 to FY28 FFB growth assumptions at 7.1 per cent, 4.8 per cent and 7.0 per cent, for now," it said.
Hap Seng Plantations's core profit improved 18.9 per cent QoQ and 59.2 per cent YoY in Q3 FY26, bringing its nine-month core earnings to RM123.24 million, up 25.8 per cent YoY.
RHB Research said this represented 76 per cent of both the research house's and consensus full-year earnings estimates.
The improvement was driven by higher FFB production, which rose five per cent YoY, helping to lower unit costs, alongside stronger crude palm oil (CPO) and palm kernel (PK) average selling prices, which increased eight per cent YoY each.
Overall, RHB Research made no changes to its earnings forecasts pending the analyst briefing scheduled for Nov 20.
It maintained its "Buy" recommendation on Hap Seng Plantations, with an unchanged target price of RM2.85.
"We believe this is justified given the company's strong ESG credentials translating into higher realised CPO and PK ASPs," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Macron's wife braves rain to climb Batu Caves [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: French President Emmanuel Macron's wife Brigitte braved heavy rain to climb the 272 steps to Batu Caves, drawing attention after a video of their visit went viral.
The brief footage, posted on TikTok by NayLinKhant yesterday, showed Brigitte climbing the staircase to Sri Subramaniar Temple, accompanied by a large entourage and tight security.
As rain poured down, members of the escort team tried to shield Brigitte from getting wet. However, she continued the climb.
Security personnel stayed close to her as other members of their entourage followed behind.
The footage attracted attention on social media, with many users impressed by her determination to complete the climb despite the wet weather.
Batu Caves, one of the country's best-known Hindu religious sites, is a limestone hill with temples. It is a major centre of worship, particularly during the annual Thaipusam festival.
The visit offered a glimpse of the First Lady of France experiencing the country's multicultural heritage and religious diversity.
Macron and his wife were in the country for a two-day official visit from Nov 16 to 17 at the invitation of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
During the visit, both countries elevated their bilateral relations to a strategic partnership, with agreements covering defence, critical minerals, energy transition, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and semiconductors.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 77 Melaka residents evacuated as floods hit three districts
Article:
MELAKA: Continuous heavy rain since yesterday evening has forced 77 residents from 20 families across three districts to evacuate to two temporary relief centres.
In a statement, the Melaka State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said Melaka Tengah recorded the highest number of evacuees, with 50 people from 13 families housed at the Japerun Pantai Kundor relief centre since 10.04pm last night.
"In Alor Gajah, 10 victims from four families were placed at the Balairaya Gadek relief centre, which opened at 1.34am today.
"Jasin recorded 17 victims from three families following flash floods since 3.30pm, though no relief centre was opened," it said.
According to the statement, four areas were hit by floods — Taman Selandar Baru, Taman Batang Melaka, Kampung Masjid Baru and Kampung Gubah — affecting 20 houses in total.
Floodwaters have begun to recede, though continuous monitoring is still being carried out by the Malaysian Civil Defence Force and related agencies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two killed, one injured in Gerik-Jeli highway crash
Article:
GERIK: Two people were killed while another was injured after a car collided with a lorry at Km49 of the Gerik-Jeli East-West Highway early today.
The victims have been identified as Normalizah Abd Manap, 36 and Razali Shakri, 45.
District police chief Superintendent Abdul Samad Othman said the accident occurred at 1.15am when a Honda Civic travelling from Jeli towards Gerik lost control while negotiating a left-hand bend.
He said the car, driven by a 36-year-old woman, then entered the opposite lane and collided with the lorry travelling from Gerik towards Jeli.
"Initial investigations found that the driver lost control after negotiating a left bend before entering the opposite lane and colliding with the lorry.
"The collision involved the front right side of the car and the right side of the lorry," he said in a statement today.
Samad said the car driver and a 45-year-old male passenger seated in the rear were confirmed dead at the scene.
"The other passenger, a 41-year-old woman seated in the front, suffered fractured ribs, while the 45-year-old lorry driver was uninjured," he said.
He said the bodies of the two victims were taken to the forensic unit at Gerik Hospital for post-mortems scheduled for 10am today.
"The car and lorry involved have been seized and sent to the Computerised Vehicle Inspection Centre (Puspakom) for inspection.
"No arrests have been made so far," he said, adding that the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which provides for offences involving causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.
He also advised road users to exercise caution, comply with traffic regulations, and practise safe, responsible driving to ensure their safety and that of other road users.
